title: 宿建德江
titleEn: Mooring for the Night on the Jiande River
author: 孟浩然
intro: A boat ties up at dusk by a misty river island, and a traveller’s loneliness comes back fresh. Only twenty characters, but the last two lines — the sky sinking below the trees, the moon coming close in the water — are among the most admired scenes in Tang poetry.
analysis: 诗人坐船漂泊在外，傍晚把船停靠在江中一个雾气笼罩的小洲旁。“日暮客愁新”是全诗的关键：天一黑，旅人的愁绪又重新涌上来。后两句只写景，却把愁写得更深。原野空旷，远远望去，天空好像比树还低；江水清澈，水中的月亮倒影好像靠近了人。“低”和“近”写的是人眼中的真实感受，空旷的天地衬出一个人的渺小，而能“亲近”他的，只有水里的月亮——这就是“借景抒情”：不直接说孤独，而让景物替人说话。全诗二十个字，前半叙事，后半写景，平静的画面里藏着很深的寂寞。
analysisEn: The poet is travelling by boat, far from home. At dusk he moors beside a small island wrapped in river mist. The key line is the second: “the day grows dark, and a traveller’s sorrow is new again” — every evening the loneliness returns as if for the first time. The last two lines say nothing about feelings at all; they simply describe what he sees, and that is exactly how they express the feeling. The open plain is so wide that, looking far off, the sky seems to sit lower than the trees. The river is so clear that the moon’s reflection seems to come right up to him. “Low” and “near” are what the eye actually experiences, not what is literally true. A vast, empty world makes one person look very small, and the only thing that comes close to keep him company is the moon in the water. Chinese critics call this technique “expressing feeling through scenery” (借景抒情): let the landscape speak for the heart. Notice the shape of the poem: two lines of story, then two lines of pure picture, with the sadness hidden inside the calm.
background: Meng Haoran (689–740) came from Xiangyang in today’s Hubei and spent most of his life as a recluse after failing to win an official post. He is traditionally thought to have written this while wandering in the southeast after that disappointment; the Jiande River is a stretch of the Xin’an River in today’s Zhejiang.
pronunciation: 渚 zhǔ（不读 zhě）。泊 bó（停船，不读 pō）。
version: 采用通行的教材版本，与《全唐诗》文本一致。

lines.lit: I move my boat and moor it by a misty islet;
lines.en: I steer the boat to a misty island and tie up for the night.

lines.lit: the sun sets, and the traveller’s sorrow is new.
lines.en: As the light fades, a traveller’s sadness wakes again.

lines.lit: The plain is wide; the sky is lower than the trees;
lines.en: The plain stretches so far the sky sinks below the trees;

lines.lit: the river is clear; the moon is near to me.
lines.en: the river is so clear the moon comes close to keep me company.

words.note: 舟：船。现代汉语说“船”，“舟”多用在成语里，如“同舟共济”。

words.en: to moor; to anchor a boat
a misty islet in the river
words.note: 烟：水上的雾气；渚：水中的小块陆地。
古义，指离家在外的人；今天“客人”是来做客的人。

words.en: the sky is lower than the trees
words.note: 低：这里是“比……低”，一个字表达比较。

words.en: the moon comes near to people
words.note: 指水中月亮的倒影离人很近。

imagery.name: 孤舟
imagery.zh: 诗人独自乘一条小船漂泊在外，停在陌生的江边过夜。
imagery.en: The poet travels alone in a small boat and spends the night moored in a strange place.

imagery.name: 夕阳
imagery.zh: “日暮”是一天里最容易想家的时候，愁绪随黄昏重新涌起。
imagery.en: Dusk is when homesickness hits hardest; the sorrow returns with the fading light.

imagery.name: 江
imagery.zh: 江水清澈，映出月亮，是诗人身边唯一的“伴”。
imagery.en: The clear river holds the moon’s reflection — the only companion beside him.

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 水中的月亮靠近他，好像在安慰这个孤独的旅人。
imagery.en: The moon in the water comes close, as if to comfort the lonely traveller.
